title: The Atmosphere The Wise Services Of Clouds Wind Rain Lightning And Thunder

questions.question: Who is being addressed by the atmosphere in this passage?
questions.answer: A traveler who has come to the world as a guest.

questions.question: What does the atmosphere invite the traveler to do?
questions.answer: It invites him to pay attention to it so he can find the One he is searching for.

questions.question: How is the atmosphere’s appearance and sound described?
questions.answer: Its appearance seems harsh yet caring, and its thunder sounds powerful but also uplifting.

questions.question: What are two important services the clouds provide for the earth?
questions.answer: They bring water to the world and help balance heat.

questions.question: How does the passage show that clouds act in an organized way?
questions.answer: They appear and disappear in a disciplined manner and gather quickly when commanded to release rain.

questions.question: What comparison is used to help explain how the clouds behave?
questions.answer: They are compared to a well-trained army that moves according to orders.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about the work of the wind?
questions.answer: He notices that it carries out many useful duties in an orderly and generous way.

questions.question: Name three tasks the air performs according to the passage.
questions.answer: It helps living things breathe, carries heat and light, and transmits sound.

questions.question: What role of the air shows its importance for plant life?
questions.answer: It helps with pollination.

questions.question: How is rain described in terms of its source and meaning?
questions.answer: It is described as coming from a hidden storehouse of mercy and as a visible sign of compassion.

questions.question: Why is rain given the name “mercy” in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it brings many caring gifts and benefits to creation.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about lightning and thunder?
questions.answer: He sees that they also have amazing duties and are not meaningless events.

questions.question: In this passage, what part of creation begins to speak to the traveler in a symbolic way?
questions.answer: The atmosphere, or the space around the earth.

questions.question: What is the traveler trying to discover through observing the atmosphere?
questions.answer: He is trying to find the One who sent him into the world.

questions.question: What feeling does the description of thunder give along with fear?
questions.answer: It also gives a sense of joy.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how clouds serve living things?
questions.answer: They deliver needed water and respond to the needs of the earth.

questions.question: How quickly do the clouds gather when it is time for rain?
questions.answer: They gather within a very short time, even within minutes.

questions.question: What does the speed of the clouds’ gathering suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests control, readiness, and obedience to command.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the air at the level of its tiny particles?
questions.answer: It describes them as if they are carrying out commands with perfect order.

questions.question: What does this description of the particles help the traveler understand?
questions.answer: It helps him see that the air is working under higher control, not by itself.

questions.question: Besides helping creatures breathe, what else does the air carry to living things?
questions.answer: It carries warmth, light, and electricity.

questions.question: What human sense is especially connected to one of the air’s functions in this passage?
questions.answer: Hearing, because the air carries sound.

questions.question: How are the raindrops described physically?
questions.answer: They are described as delicate, shining, and sweet.

questions.question: What does the traveler understand about rain from these qualities?
questions.answer: He understands that rain is full of mercy and benefit.

questions.question: What broader conclusion can be drawn from the cloud, wind, rain, and lightning together?
questions.answer: They all work with wisdom and purpose, showing the order and care of the Creator.

questions.question: What message does the atmosphere give the traveler at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It tells him that by looking at it, he can reach the truth he is seeking.

questions.question: Why might the atmosphere be described as both rough and gentle?
questions.answer: Because it can seem severe in power but still serves creation with kindness.

questions.question: What does watering the world’s garden mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means the clouds provide rain that supports life on earth.

questions.question: How do the clouds help make the earth suitable for life besides sending rain?
questions.answer: They reduce excessive heat.

questions.question: What detail shows that the clouds are not acting randomly?
questions.answer: They withdraw completely at times and then return quickly when needed.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the comparison between clouds and an obedient army?
questions.answer: Their movement follows order and command rather than chance.

questions.question: How is the air shown to be beneficial to all living things?
questions.answer: It supports breathing and delivers things necessary for life.

questions.question: Which function of the air connects different creatures or places to one another?
questions.answer: Its carrying of sound connects them.

questions.question: Why is pollination mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: To show that even plant life depends on the careful work done through the air.

questions.question: What does the image of rain coming from a hidden treasury suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that its source is beyond human control and full of mercy.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes rain more than just a weather event?
questions.answer: It carries gifts, benefits, and compassion for creation.

questions.question: How does the final mention of lightning and thunder support the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows that even dramatic atmospheric events serve meaningful purposes.

questions.question: What does the passage say the traveler can discover through the atmosphere?
questions.answer: He can discover the One he is seeking and the One who sent him.

questions.question: What makes the clouds an example of wisdom and mercy?
questions.answer: They provide life-giving water, balance heat, and rush to help where needed.

questions.question: In what way do the clouds act like a trained group under command?
questions.answer: They sometimes disappear completely and then quickly assemble when ordered.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the clouds waiting for more orders suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that they are under control and do not act independently.

questions.question: What impression does the traveler get from observing the wind?
questions.answer: He sees it as a servant carrying out many duties with order and generosity.

questions.question: How does the passage emphasize the wide range of the air’s service?
questions.answer: It mentions many different tasks for animals, plants, and communication.

questions.question: What are two examples of how the air supports life directly?
questions.answer: It enables breathing and carries needed energy such as warmth and light.

questions.question: What does the air do that supports life indirectly through plants?
questions.answer: It assists in pollination.

questions.question: What view of rain is encouraged by calling it a form of mercy?
questions.answer: It encourages people to see rain as a compassionate gift rather than just a natural process.

questions.question: What does the description of raindrops suggest about the care behind their creation?
questions.answer: It suggests beauty, precision, and kindness.

questions.question: How are lightning and thunder treated in relation to the rest of the atmosphere?
questions.answer: They are also presented as carrying out remarkable tasks.

questions.question: What central truth ties together clouds, wind, rain, and lightning in this passage?
questions.answer: All of them show deliberate order and point to a wise and merciful Creator.

questions.question: From what perspective does the passage examine the atmosphere?
questions.answer: It examines it through the reflections of a traveler observing creation.

questions.question: What is the atmosphere said to declare to the traveler?
questions.answer: It declares that it can lead him to the One he is seeking.

questions.question: How does the traveler respond to the atmosphere’s call?
questions.answer: He looks at it and listens carefully to what its signs reveal.

questions.question: Why are the clouds important for “the garden of the world”?
questions.answer: They nourish the earth by bringing water needed for life.

questions.question: How do the clouds show mercy toward the earth’s inhabitants?
questions.answer: They provide water, reduce harsh heat, and hurry to where help is needed.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the clouds can fill the sky and then vanish?
questions.answer: It suggests impressive power joined with strict order and discipline.

questions.question: Why is the military comparison effective in describing the clouds?
questions.answer: It highlights obedience, coordination, and readiness.

questions.question: What idea is conveyed by saying the air’s tiny parts act as if they receive commands?
questions.answer: It conveys that the air’s actions are purposeful and directed.

questions.question: How does the air benefit both humans and other creatures?
questions.answer: It helps all living things breathe and supplies what they need for life.

questions.question: What service of the air is related to communication?
questions.answer: It carries sound.

questions.question: What does the phrase “hidden treasury of mercy” teach about rain?
questions.answer: It teaches that rain is a precious gift sent with compassion.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect rain with mercy instead of only with water?
questions.answer: Because rain contains many benefits and comes in a caring way to sustain life.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the short statement about lightning and thunder?
questions.answer: They also serve wise purposes, even if those purposes are not fully explained there.

questions.question: What role does the traveler play in the passage?
questions.answer: He acts as an observer who learns about the Creator by studying the atmosphere.

questions.question: What claim does the atmosphere make about itself to the traveler?
questions.answer: It claims that it can guide him to the truth he is looking for.

questions.question: How are the atmosphere’s outward features presented in a balanced way?
questions.answer: They are shown as strong and awe-inspiring, yet also helpful and life-serving.

questions.question: What practical blessings come through the clouds?
questions.answer: Water for life, relief from heat, and help for places in need.

questions.question: What scene shows the clouds’ readiness to obey?
questions.answer: They quickly gather and cover the sky when it is time for rain.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying the clouds wait for further orders?
questions.answer: It implies they are under authority and act according to command.

questions.question: Why does the traveler focus on the many tasks of the wind?
questions.answer: To understand that such wide and careful service cannot be meaningless.

questions.question: What does the wind provide besides movement in the air?
questions.answer: It helps carry breath, warmth, light, electricity, and sound.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the atmosphere serves plant life as well as animal life?
questions.answer: It helps pollinate plants.

questions.question: How is rain portrayed emotionally as well as physically?
questions.answer: It is portrayed as beautiful drops that carry compassion and care.

questions.question: Why is calling rain “mercy” an important interpretation in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it presents rain as a sign of divine kindness toward creation.

questions.question: What is the traveler able to recognize about lightning and thunder?
questions.answer: He recognizes that they also have amazing functions.

questions.question: What overall conclusion about the atmosphere does this passage lead the reader toward?
questions.answer: Its events are organized, beneficial, and meaningful, showing the wisdom and mercy of Allah.
